P1_fx_receipts.question: Can resident individuals receive foreign currency for services or digital exports? Any conversion or repatriation rule?
P1_fx_receipts.answer: Partly established. Exporters keep 70% of gross export proceeds and must sell 30% to the Reserve Bank at the interbank rate (FXD5/2026, March 2026). Foreign currency received by individuals has historically been treated as 'free funds', held in Nostro FCA accounts and not surrendered (2019 RBZ circular). Whether payments from foreign clients to an individual freelancer count as free funds or as service-export proceeds (30% surrender) was not confirmed.
P1_fx_receipts.note: Surrender rule from a bank's summary of FXD5/2026 (one domain); free-funds rule from 2019 press; no current RBZ text on individual service exporters found on 2026-10-22.

P2_fcy_account.question: Can resident individuals hold a foreign-currency account locally?
P2_fcy_account.answer: Yes. Foreign-currency (Nostro FCA) accounts are standard in Zimbabwe; free funds received by individuals are held in Nostro FCAs (2019 circular). The economy is largely USD-based alongside the ZiG.
P2_fcy_account.note: Only a 2019 press summary captured; no current RBZ text on resident FCA accounts captured on 2026-10-22.

L1_registration.question: Must an individual register a business to sell digital services/products? Simplest legal form?
L1_registration.answer: A sole trader does not need to register with the Companies Registry. The key step is mandatory tax registration with ZIMRA for anyone carrying on a trade or business, done online via the TaRMS Self-Service Portal. A guide says there is no specific fee beyond obtaining the tax identifier.

L2_tax_id.question: Tax ID: who needs one, how to get it?
L2_tax_id.answer: A Taxpayer Identification Number (TIN), issued on successful registration on ZIMRA's TaRMS Self-Service Portal. It replaced the older Business Partner (BP) number. A tax clearance certificate (ITF263) is tied to the TIN.

L3_income_tax_foreign.question: Income tax on foreign-source income for residents; rates or special regimes
L3_income_tax_foreign.answer: Zimbabwe taxes on a source basis: income from a source within (or deemed within) Zimbabwe is taxed whatever the residence. Under case law (CIR v Lever Bros), the source is where the work that earns the income is done. A freelancer working from Zimbabwe for foreign clients is therefore likely taxable in Zimbabwe, while foreign income not deemed Zimbabwean is not. Presumptive taxes apply to some small businesses. Individual rates were reported up to 40%.
L3_income_tax_foreign.note: Single secondary domain (Alliott Global) for the source rule; ZIMRA tax tables and Income Tax Act not read on 2026-10-22; PwC Zimbabwe page 404.

sources.title: Taxation Law in Zimbabwe - an overview
sources.quote: Thus, generally, all receipts (not of a capital nature) arising from a source within Zimbabwe are taxed, irrespective of the residential status of the taxpayer.

sources.title: Taxation Law in Zimbabwe - an overview
sources.quote: In CIR v Lever Bros and Unilever Ltd (1946) the applicable principle was that the source of receipts, received as income, is not where they come from, but the originating cause of their being received as income is the work which the taxpayer does to earn them.

L3_income_tax_foreign.notes: Application to remote freelancing is an inference from the Lever Bros principle.

L4_vat_gst.question: VAT/GST: rate, registration threshold, treatment of exported digital services
L4_vat_gst.answer: Standard VAT 15.5%, up from 15% from 1 Jan 2026 (Finance Act 2025); many older pages still say 15%. Compulsory registration applies when taxable supplies exceed US$25,000 in 12 months. Since 2026, input-tax claims need FDMS-validated (fiscalised) invoices. Treatment of exported services was not established.

L5_data_protection.question: Data-protection law applicable to a small online business
L5_data_protection.answer: Cyber and Data Protection Act, with POTRAZ as the Data Protection Authority. Under SI 155 of 2024, organisations processing personal data of 50 or more people need an annual data-controller licence. It costs US$50 a year for 50–1,000 people, and US$300 plus a US$30 application fee for 1,001–100,000. A certified Data Protection Officer must be appointed. POTRAZ began mandatory compliance inspections from 1 Sep 2026.
L5_data_protection.note: Single secondary domain (CITE) captured; techzim (HTTP 520) and The Independent (404) failed on 2026-10-22; SI 155 of 2024 text not read.

L6_consumer_ecommerce.question: Consumer-protection / e-commerce rules for online sales (refunds, disclosures)
L6_consumer_ecommerce.answer: Under the Consumer Protection Act 2019 (s. 53), consumers may cancel any electronic transaction without reason or penalty within seven days of receiving the goods or concluding the agreement. The only allowed charge is the direct cost of returning goods, and prepaid amounts must be refunded within fourteen days of cancellation.

W1_workarounds.question: Simple, legal routes around payment barriers for a beginner (no misrepresentation, nominees or sanctions evasion)
W1_workarounds.answer: Barriers: Stripe does not accept merchants here; platforms that pay out through PayPal Payouts cannot pay PayPal accounts here (not on PayPal's Payouts list, see P4 for ordinary PayPal receiving); Wise does not let residents hold money. Simple legal routes: (1) Sell digital products or software through a merchant of record: Dodo Payments. The platform is the legal seller to your customers, handles card payments and consumer VAT/sales tax, and pays you out. You still declare the payouts as your income at home (see L3). (2) Sell services on Upwork, which is available here (not on its restricted list). Which withdrawal methods you get (bank, PayPal, Payoneer, etc.) depends on the country and shows in your account. (3) Creator income through the YouTube Partner Program (available here). (4) Paid apps and in-app sales through Google Play (merchant registration available here). (5) For direct clients, a bank transfer (SWIFT) into your own local account always works. Follow the local foreign-exchange rules (see P1) and keep invoices. Avoid: opening accounts with a foreign address, a relative's or friend's identity, or a VPN to look like you are elsewhere. It breaches platform terms (accounts and funds get frozen) and can break anti-money-laundering or sanctions law.
